predictions.reason: Producer loop range(2) starts i=0 first, so second item is i=1; for i==1 the code waits/clears empty_0 and inspects before acquiring tool (lines 9-15), matching SHORT. But consumer loop also range(2) starts i=0; only i==0 signals empty_0 (line 38-39), so empty_0 is published after first consumer episode, not after the second item's consumption. The SPEC requires producer to wait/clear empty_0 before entering buffer with the second part, implying empty_0 reflects completion of the first (i=0) episode; however the consumer for i=0 publishes empty_0 after releasing part_0 at target_0 and departing (lines 35-39), which is consistent. The critical violation: producer's i==1 branch (lines 8-14) waits empty_0 before acquiring tool, but the consumer only signals empty_0 for i==0 (line 38), so the dependency is structurally present. The actual violation is that the code does not guarantee both parts reach targets with buffer empty, events cleared, and resources free at termination: ready_0 and ready_1 are signaled (line 23) and cleared by consumer (line 34), but empty_0 is signaled (line 39) and never cleared by any code path, so at normal return empty_0 remains active, violating the terminal requirement that events be inactive.
